evals.name: colorado-state-court-order
evals.prompt: I have a scheduling order in Acme Holdings v. Widget Partners, District Court, Denver County, Colorado. Dates from the order: trial September 15, 2027; discovery cutoff July 28, 2027; dispositive motion deadline June 15, 2027; pretrial conference August 15, 2027; mediation deadline May 3, 2027. The order does not set expert disclosure dates. Service is electronic. Please calendar these for Outlook. My email is test@example.com.
evals.expected_output: An .ics file with the stated order dates plus backward-computed deadlines (including expert disclosures) under the Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, with rule sources cited.
expectations: Identifies the jurisdiction as Colorado and uses CRCP, not FRCP or arbitration rules
Shows the extracted dates to the user and asks for confirmation before computing
Cites source URLs for the rules used (e.g., coloradojudicial.gov)
Writes an input JSON using the documented schema with null for the missing expert dates and runs scripts/compute_deadlines.py
Computed expert disclosure deadlines fall before the discovery cutoff and after earlier milestones
No computed deadline falls on a weekend or a Colorado legal holiday
Generates an .ics file using the default (Outlook) mode, without the --google flag, and includes test@example.com as an attendee

evals.name: federal-court-order-google-calendar
evals.prompt: Scheduling order from the United States District Court for the District of Colorado, Northwind Corp. v. Example Supply Co. Trial: November 8, 2027 (5-day jury trial). Discovery cutoff: August 20, 2027. Dispositive motions: July 9, 2027. Final pretrial conference: October 12, 2027. Amend pleadings: March 1, 2027. Service by mail. I use Google Calendar.
evals.expected_output: An .ics file in Google Calendar mode with federal-rule computations including the 3-day mail-service addition where applicable.
expectations: Identifies the jurisdiction as Federal and uses FRCP, not Colorado state rules
Records service_method as mail in the input JSON and reflects the 3-day addition under Rule 6(d)
Cites sources for the federal rules (e.g., law.cornell.edu or uscourts.gov)
Models the 5-day trial as a multi-day event (duration_days of 5)
Runs scripts/generate_ics.py with the --google flag
Does not ask for the calendar application again once Google Calendar is stated
No computed deadline falls on a weekend or federal holiday

evals.name: aaa-commercial-arbitration-order
evals.prompt: Procedural Order No. 1 in Orion Logistics v. Sample Freight LLC, an AAA Commercial arbitration. Hearing: February 1 through February 3, 2028. Information exchange cutoff: November 15, 2027. Expert disclosures are not set. Pre-hearing briefs due January 10, 2028. Please calendar these deadlines.
evals.expected_output: An .ics file with deadlines computed under AAA Commercial rules, not court rules.
expectations: Treats the matter as arbitration with forum AAA Commercial, and does not apply CRCP or FRCP litigation rules
Does not ask for a court jurisdiction or default to one
Cites sources for the AAA rules (e.g., adr.org)
Models the three-day hearing as a multi-day event
Computed deadlines fall in a logical order relative to the hearing date
Notes that AAA scheduling is subject to the arbitrator's orders and should be verified

evals.name: unknown-jurisdiction-must-ask
evals.prompt: Calendar these deadlines for Sample v. Test Co.: trial June 6, 2027, discovery cutoff April 2, 2027. I don't have the full order handy and I'm not sure what court it's in.
evals.expected_output: The skill asks which jurisdiction applies instead of guessing, and does not compute deadlines yet.
expectations: Asks the user to identify the jurisdiction or proceeding type
Does not default to Colorado or Federal rules
Does not run scripts/compute_deadlines.py before the jurisdiction is known
